core_obligations: Clause (i): put R = O[A,B]O and consider the quotient O/R; since A and B generate O and commute modulo R, the quotient is commutative, so the canonical map kills [O,O] and therefore [O,O] is contained in R (proof lines 3066-3079).

Clause (ii): in the third displayed equation of the cited theorem the right-hand side is a nonzero scalar multiple of [A,B] gamma, while the left-hand side equals [A^2,B^2] + (q^2+q^{-2})[B,ABA], which lies in [O,O]; hence [A,B] gamma lies in [O,O] as well (proof lines 3081-3092).
Clause (iii): combine clauses (i) and (ii) with the centrality of gamma to get O[A,B]O gamma contained in O[A,B]O (proof lines 3094-3095).
proof_roadmap: Prove the first inclusion by making the quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by [A,B] commutative (proof lines 3066-3079).
Compare the two sides of the alternating-presentation relation to place [A,B] gamma in the commutator subspace, and finish the third clause with centrality of gamma (proof lines 3081-3095).
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes three inclusions relating the commutator subspace of the algebra O to the two-sided ideal generated by [A,B], and to its behaviour under multiplication by the central element gamma (statement lines 3049-3064). The first clause is proved by a quotient argument: dividing by O[A,B]O makes the generating pair A, B commute, so the quotient is commutative and the canonical map annihilates every commutator (proof lines 3066-3079). The second clause computes both sides of the alternating-presentation relation, whose right-hand side is a nonzero scalar multiple of [A,B] gamma while the left-hand side is visibly a sum of commutators (proof lines 3081-3092). The third clause then combines the two with the centrality of gamma in a single line. The content is in the first two clauses, each of which is an honest short argument rather than a citation. H2.
